speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with yellowish discoloration of the skin; have you noticed if this jaundice appears within the first 24 hours of life?

REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_Total_Serum. REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_Direct_Serum.

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born full term at 38 weeks via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. No past medical history. Social history: Exclusive breastfeeding every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Patient
text: No reported changes in bowel habits or urination. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that acute appendicitis is not a diagnosis for a newborn presenting with jaundice; let's focus on the bilirubin levels. While we wait for those results, have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools? REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_Total_Serum. REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_Direct_Serum.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results show a total bilirubin of 7 mg/dL with an indirect fraction of 6.4 mg/dL, confirming unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Since the levels are relatively low and unconjugated, is the infant feeding well and gaining weight appropriately? Also, please tell me if you have any history of blood type incompatibility or a family history of jaundice.

REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_Differential. REQUEST TEST: G6PD_Assay. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Type_and_Coombs.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 17.6 g/dL, Reticulocytes: 0.3%, Bilirubin_Total: 7 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.6 mg/dL, Maternal_Blood_Group: A, Rh-negative, Fetal_Blood_Group: 0, Rh-positive, Free_T4: 7 μg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results confirm unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal reticulocyte count and free T4, ruling out hemolytic anemia and hypothyroidism; however, the blood group incompatibility (Mother A Rh-negative, Fetal O Rh-positive) makes ABO incompatibility unlikely. Has the mother received Rh immune globulin, and is the infant experiencing excessive sleepiness or poor feeding despite the current stable labs?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological Jaundice
